decision.title: Retain the compatible parser despite a faster alternative
decision.summary: A proposed parser is faster in a synthetic benchmark but changes how valid existing documents are interpreted. Keep the current parser. A faster implementation can be reconsidered when it preserves the supported input contract and has a verified recovery path.
decision.request: Confirm the supported input contract and the owner of any future compatibility change.

model.explanation: A parser turns a document into data used by callers. The same output shape can hide a change in meaning.
model.behavior: Current callers continue to receive the existing interpretation of supported documents.
model.architecture: The candidate replaces the parsing function behind the same library interface; downstream callers would otherwise receive changed values without changing their code.

options.tradeoff: Slower on the synthetic benchmark but preserves the supported behavior.

options.description: Replace it with the faster parser
options.tradeoff: Lower measured time on synthetic inputs but changed interpretation for a supported input.

comparison.whySelected: The compatibility floor is unmet. The benchmark cannot justify silently changing downstream behavior.

falsifiers.condition: The candidate preserves all supported meanings on independent compatibility inputs and improves representative workloads
falsifiers.response: Reopen the proposal with those results and recovery evidence

evidence.finding: The synthetic benchmark completes earlier with the candidate.
The synthetic compatibility case produces a different value for a supported document.
Reverting the dependency in the simulation restores the previous interpretation.

claims.statement: The candidate is faster on the supplied synthetic inputs
claims.limits: No downstream workload improvement has been demonstrated.

claims.statement: The candidate changes a supported document interpretation
claims.limits: The example does not establish how many real consumers depend on that case.

claims.statement: Downstream callers may silently change behavior
claims.scope: Callers relying on the changed interpretation

failureModes.failure: A caller receives a changed value without an API error
failureModes.signal: Compatibility fixtures differ or consumers report changed interpretation
failureModes.response: Stop adoption and retain or restore the previous dependency

observe.where: Compatibility suite results and consumer issue reports for the exact revision

stop.when: Any supported input changes meaning unexpectedly
stop.action: Stop the release or downstream adoption through the existing release process

rollback.action: Restore the prior library revision using the reviewed dependency rollback process
rollback.verification: Run the compatibility suite and the affected consumer workflow after the restore

unknowns.question: Which consumers rely on the changed interpretation?
unknowns.impact: A silent change may affect consumers absent from the test corpus
unknowns.nextStep: Collect representative compatibility examples before proposing a contract change

unknowns.question: Will every supported consumer recover after a dependency revert?
unknowns.impact: Persistent derived data may require separate repair
unknowns.nextStep: Verify consumer recovery before authorizing adoption

humanDecisions.question: Should the supported input contract change in a future breaking release?
